collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IV: ROMANCE, COURTSHIP AND WEDDINGS (LCD-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Crushes and courting on Isola: wondering whether someone likes you back, flowers and love songs, first dates, serenades gone wrong, proposals, weddings big and small, how many children, breakups and starting over.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A shy villager asks a grandparent how to tell someone they love them: take the old advice, or find their own way.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has loved someone in the village for a long time and has never said a word. (subject.He/she) finally asks (subject.his/her) grandparent, (friend), how (friend.he/she) courted (friend.his/her) own sweetheart, sixty years ago. (friend)'s advice is to stand on a rock in front of the whole village and shout it. (subject) is horrified. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) stands on a rock at the gathering and shouts it. The whole village goes silent. The person (subject.he/she) loves stands up, walks over, and says, "You could have just asked." Then (other.he/she) says yes anyway. (friend) is insufferable about it for a month.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) thanks (friend) and finds a quieter way: a basket of the best fruit, left at a door, with a note. It works, slowly. When (friend) hears, (friend.he/she) says it was very dull, and that (friend.he/she) is delighted.
